cues.en: (gentle music)
cues.zh: （輕柔音樂）

cues.en: Instructor: Welcome back everyone to this lecture on the perceptron model.
cues.zh: 歡迎大家回來，本堂介紹感知器模型。

cues.en: To begin understanding deep learning, we're gonna start by actually building up our model abstractions.
cues.zh: 理解深度學習，先建立模型的抽象概念。

cues.en: We're gonna be begin by exploring what real single biological neurons look like.
cues.zh: 先探索真實單一生物神經元的樣子。

cues.en: Then we'll model those mathematically as a single perceptron, see how we can group together perceptrons, or artificial neurons, to build out a multi-layer perceptron model.
cues.zh: 再數學化成單一感知器，看看如何把感知器，也就是人工神經元，組成多層模型。

cues.en: And then see how that expands to a deep learning neural network framework.
cues.zh: 再擴展到深度學習神經網路框架。

cues.en: So as we learn more about complex models, we'll also then introduce some key mathematical concepts to the actual mathematical functionality of those neurons.
cues.zh: 隨複雜模型介紹，加入神經元數學功能的重要概念，

cues.en: And that is things like activation functions, gradient descent, and backpropagation.
cues.zh: 例如激活函數、梯度下降、反向傳播。

cues.en: But right, right now we're gonna focus on just building out that single perceptron model based off a real biological neuron.
cues.zh: 但現在只專注根據真實神經元，建單一感知器。

cues.en: So if the whole idea behind deep learning is to have computers artificially mimic biological and natural intelligence, it's probably a good idea that we should build a general understanding
cues.zh: 深度學習想讓電腦人工模仿生物與自然智慧，因此最好先大致理解

cues.en: of how biological neurons work.
cues.zh: 生物神經元運作。

cues.en: So here we can see some real stained neurons in a cerebral cortex, and basically what we're gonna attempt to do is check out the way these biological neurons work
cues.zh: 這裡是大腦皮質中染色的真實神經元，想看如何運作，

cues.en: and see if we can develop a simplified abstraction off these real neurons.
cues.zh: 建立簡化抽象。

cues.en: So here's a illustration of biological neurons and you can see that there is a lot going on.
cues.zh: 這是神經元圖解，可看到很多內容。

cues.en: And don't worry, this isn't a biology class.
cues.zh: 別擔心，不是生物課。

cues.en: And the main things we're gonna focus on is just the neuron itself.
cues.zh: 主要專注神經元本身。

cues.en: So the main things to see here is that there's some sort of nucleus or center to this neuron.
cues.zh: 重點是某種細胞核或中心，

cues.en: There's the cell body, and it looks like we have both inputs and outputs or axons spreading out from this nucleus.
cues.zh: 有細胞體，似乎有從中心延伸的輸入、輸出或軸突。

cues.en: So let's take this illustration of a biological neuron.
cues.zh: 取這張圖，

cues.en: And what we're gonna do is we're gonna really simplify this and we're gonna simplify it so much that I will actually create my own illustration.
cues.zh: 大幅簡化，簡單到我自己畫。

cues.en: And I'm definitely not an artist.
cues.zh: 我絕對不是藝術家。

cues.en: This is an extremely kind of rough illustration, but don't worry, you'll see why I drew it like this later on in this lecture.
cues.zh: 畫得很粗糙，但稍後就知道為何這樣畫。

cues.en: But the main thing we wanna focus off the biological components are the dendrites.
cues.zh: 生物部分主要專注樹突，

cues.en: And we can think of those as input going into the main nucleus of this neuron.
cues.zh: 可想成進入神經元中心核的輸入。

cues.en: And then the axon, which is some sort of output.
cues.zh: 軸突是某種輸出。

cues.en: Now, again, this isn't 100% biologically correct, but this feeds into our perceptron model.
cues.zh: 再次，不是百分百生物正確，但能連到感知器。

cues.en: Basically, we're gonna think of neurons, biologically, as accepting some sort of input signal and the input signal can come from a variety of sources,
cues.zh: 基本上把神經元想成接受某種輸入訊號，可來自多種來源，

cues.en: and then we'll do some sort of calculation in the nucleus or something happens in the nucleus of this neuron, and then it outputs as a single output axon.
cues.zh: 再在核做計算、發生某件事，最後由單一軸突輸出。

cues.en: And that can then lead over to another nucleus as the dendrite to another neuron.
cues.zh: 可連到另一神經元的核，作為其樹突輸入。

cues.en: Now how do we take this very simplified biological neuron model and convert it into a mathematical model?
cues.zh: 如何把簡化生物模型轉數學模型？

cues.en: This is where the idea of the perceptron comes in.
cues.zh: 這就用感知器。

cues.en: A perceptron was a form of neural network introduced all the way back in 1958 by Frank Rosenblatt.
cues.zh: Frank Rosenblatt 在 1958 年提出的神經網路形式。

cues.en: And amazingly, even back then in the 1950s, he saw huge potential, stating, "A perceptron may eventually be able to learn, make decisions, and translate languages."
cues.zh: 驚人的是，1950 年代就看到潛力，表示感知器最終或許能學習、決策、翻譯語言。

cues.en: And if you have ever used something like Google Translate, Google Translate actually uses a neural network as its main way of converting from one language to another.
cues.zh: 用過 Google Translate 的話，它其實以神經網路作主要語言轉換方式。

cues.en: And Frank Rosenblatt actually saw the perceptron as one of the main base units to building out that sort of technology.
cues.zh: Rosenblatt 把感知器視為建立這種技術的主要基本單元。

cues.en: And he thought of this all the way back in the late 1950s.
cues.zh: 1950 年代末就這樣想。

cues.en: However, about a decade later, in the late 1960s, two researchers, Marvin Minsky and Seymour Papert, they published the book labeled "Perceptrons."
cues.zh: 但十年後，1960 年代末，Marvin Minsky、Seymour Papert 出版《Perceptrons》。

cues.en: And it suggested that there were actually severe limitations to what perceptrons would be able to do.
cues.zh: 認為感知器能力有嚴重限制。

cues.en: And a big part of that limitation was the actual computational power necessary to work with multi-layer perceptron models.
cues.zh: 很大限制在多層感知器需要的計算能力。

cues.en: So back in the late 1960s, there wasn't really enough computational power to actually make full use of the idea of the perceptron mathematical model.
cues.zh: 1960 年代末沒有足夠算力，充分運用數學模型。

cues.en: And this publication, this book, actually marks the beginning of what's known as the AI Winter where very little funding went into research in artificial intelligence and neural networks in the 1970s.
cues.zh: 這本書標誌所謂 AI 寒冬開始，1970 年代人工智慧與神經網路研究資金很少。

cues.en: So that's why, even though this idea was spawned in the late 1950s, it's taken up to the modern age to actually fully implement neural networks.
cues.zh: 所以想法雖源於1950年代末，直到現代才完整實作。

cues.en: Now, fortunately for us, we already now live in the present and we know the amazing power of neural networks, which all really stem from this simple perceptron model that was created all the way back in 1958.
cues.zh: 幸好活在現在，知道神經網路驚人能力，都源自1958年的簡單感知器。

cues.en: So let's go ahead and head back and convert that simple biological neuron model into the perceptron model, and then go through a simple example of how a perceptron model works.
cues.zh: 回去把簡單生物模型轉感知器，再看運作例子。

cues.en: So recall, we have a very simplified biological neuron model.
cues.zh: 記得簡化生物模型，

cues.en: So this is the biological neuron, modeled in a very simple fashion, where we have incoming dendrites, then some sort of center nucleus, and a single output to the axon.
cues.zh: 有進入的樹突、中央細胞核、單一軸突輸出。

cues.en: So what we're gonna do is, instead, we're gonna replace these biological units with some mathematical ones.
cues.zh: 改用數學單元取代。

cues.en: So what we're gonna do is we're gonna define some set of inputs going into this single point, which we'll call the neuron, and then has that single output.
cues.zh: 定義一組輸入進單點，叫神經元，再單一輸出。

cues.en: So let's go ahead and work through a simple example of how the simple perceptron model actually works.
cues.zh: 看簡單感知器例子。

cues.en: What we're gonna do is we're gonna imagine, essentially, two data points, X1 and X2.
cues.zh: 想像兩個資料點 X1、X2。

cues.en: So these two variables, X1 and X2, are going into as input into this perceptron.
cues.zh: 兩變數作為輸入。

cues.en: And you can imagine that, inside this perceptron, that neuron is gonna have some sort of function.
cues.zh: 感知器裡有某種函數。

cues.en: So it's gonna have some sort of functionality and perform something on those inputs of X.
cues.zh: 對輸入 X 執行某種功能，

cues.en: And it's going to then output some Y.
cues.zh: 再輸出 Y。

cues.en: So we have some function in the neuron, takes in these X values, performs something on them, and then outputs Y.
cues.zh: 函數接受 X、運算、輸出 Y。

cues.en: So if F of X, that function, is just a sum, then Y is equal to X1 plus X2.
cues.zh: 若 f(X) 只是加總，Y=X1+X2。

cues.en: And this is a very, very simplified perceptron model.
cues.zh: 非常簡化。

cues.en: Later on, we'll expand on this with activation functions.
cues.zh: 稍後擴展激活函數。

cues.en: But for right now, this is just showing you how we can go from a biological neuron to a perceptron model.
cues.zh: 現在只展示生物神經元怎麼變感知器。

cues.en: So we have these inputs, X1 and X2, we push them through some sort of function of X, and then we output some Y.
cues.zh: 有 X1、X2 輸入，經 f(X)，輸出 Y。

cues.en: So realistically, we would want to be able to adjust some parameter in order for the perceptron to learn.
cues.zh: 實際希望調某參數，讓感知器學習。

cues.en: Right now, there's no real way for the perceptron to adjust its ability to learn to kind of correct the output of Y.
cues.zh: 現在無法調整學習能力、修正輸出 Y。

cues.en: So what we can do is we can add in adjustable weights that will multiply against these inputs of X.
cues.zh: 可以加可調權重，乘上輸入 X。

cues.en: So we're gonna say here is that we'll take in each input of X and apply it to its own weight and then we can adjust that weight as necessary
cues.zh: 每個 X 有自己的權重，視需要調整，

cues.en: in order to get the correct value of Y or the expected value of Y that maybe we're performing some sort of supervised learning on.
cues.zh: 取得正確或預期 Y，例如監督式學習。

cues.en: So maybe we're trying to solve a regression task where Y is the actual continuous label we're trying to predict, or maybe we're doing classification and Y is a category.
cues.zh: 可能迴歸，Y 是連續標籤；或分類，Y 是類別。

cues.en: But the most important part here is we're gonna need to be able to take this perception model and adjust it somehow in order to get the correct value of Y.
cues.zh: 最重要的是能調整感知器，得到正確 Y。

cues.en: And one way we can do this is by applying a weight to each input and then we can adjust the weight.
cues.zh: 一種方法是各輸入加權，再調權重。

cues.en: So we'll label these weights corresponding to their inputs as W1 for X1 and W2 for X2.
cues.zh: 對應標為 X1 的 W1、X2 的 W2。

cues.en: Which means if our function, still simplified. is just an addition, we'll say Y is equal to X1 times W1 plus X2 times W2.
cues.zh: 函數仍簡化成加總，Y=X1×W1+X2×W2。

cues.en: Now we could update the weights in order to affect the output Y.
cues.zh: 更新權重就影響 Y。

cues.en: But what happens if X input is actually zero?
cues.zh: 但 X 輸入為 0 呢？

cues.en: That means no matter what you do to the weight, that actually won't change anything.
cues.zh: 不管怎麼調權重，都不會變。

cues.en: So to fix that problem, we could add in a bias term B to the inputs.
cues.zh: 可以在輸入加偏差項 B。

cues.en: So regardless if X1 is zero or X2 is zero, which means that when you multiply it by a weight, it'll always end up being zero regardless of how you update the weight.
cues.zh: 不論 X1 或 X2 是 0，乘權重總是 0，不管怎麼更新。

cues.en: What we can do is we can add in a bias term B to the inputs.
cues.zh: 可以加偏差 B。

cues.en: So we essentially assign this neuron its own particular bias so that the inputs end up not just getting multiplied by a weight, but having a bias added to them.
cues.zh: 替神經元指定偏差，輸入不只乘權重，也加偏差。

cues.en: And keep in mind the weights can be positive or negative and the biases can also be positive or negative.
cues.zh: 記得權重可正可負，偏差也一樣。

cues.en: A good way to think about the bias is that the multiplication or the product of X1 times W1, or the input times its weight, has to overcome the bias value
cues.zh: 可以想成 X1×W1，輸入乘權重，必須克服偏差值，

cues.en: in order to start having an effect on the output of Y.
cues.zh: 才開始影響 Y。

cues.en: So here, for this very simple example, we end up approximating the output of Y to be equal to X1 times W1 plus B plus X2 times W2 plus B.
cues.zh: 這個簡單例子，Y 約等於 X1×W1+B+X2×W2+B。

cues.en: And this is just a very simple summation that's happening inside the neuron.
cues.zh: 只是神經元裡的簡單加總。

cues.en: Later on, we'll talk about more realistic activation functions that you'll have in typical networks.
cues.zh: 之後會談一般網路更實際的激活函數。

cues.en: Keep in mind, we can expand this to a generalization for a variety of inputs all the way to some input N.
cues.zh: 可概括到多種輸入，一直到 N。

cues.en: And so now we've been able to see how we can model a biological neuron as a simple perceptron.
cues.zh: 現在看到生物神經元如何建模成感知器。

cues.en: And mathematically, our generalization was simply starting at I is equal to one, all the way to N at number of inputs.
cues.zh: 數學上從 i=1 到 N 個輸入，

cues.en: We simply grabbed that particular input value, multiply it by some weight, that later on we'll be adjusting, plus a bias value.
cues.zh: 取輸入值、乘稍後調整的權重，再加偏差。

cues.en: Later on, we're actually going to see how we can expand this model to have X be a tensor of information where a tensor is an n-dimensional matrix.
cues.zh: 稍後把 X 擴成資訊張量，也就是 n 維矩陣。

cues.en: So let's review what we've learned so far.
cues.zh: 複習。

cues.en: We understand the very, very basics of a biological neuron, the fact that there's dendrites providing input to a nucleus and then some axon as a single output.
cues.zh: 懂最基本生物神經元，樹突輸入到核、單一軸突輸出。

cues.en: And what we've been able to do is take the research done in the late 1950s of the simple perceptron model and create a very simple mathematical model replicating those core concepts behind a neuron
cues.zh: 用1950年代末感知器研究，建立簡單數學模型，複製核心概念，

cues.en: where we have inputs, we apply some sort of weight to them, as well as adding a bias term, pass them through some sort of function, and then we get out that single output.
cues.zh: 輸入、加權、加偏差、通過函數、得到單一輸出。

cues.en: So let's go ahead and then in the next lecture learn how we can expand a single perceptron to a full neural network.
cues.zh: 下一堂看單一感知器如何擴成完整網路。

cues.en: And then we'll see how we can add in more complex ideas such as activation functions, cost functions, and then see how that works with a feedforward network as well as back propagation.
cues.zh: 再加激活函數、成本函數，看看如何搭配前饋網路與反向傳播。

cues.en: Okay, thanks and I'll see you at the next lecture.
cues.zh: 好，謝謝，下一堂見。
